sn11.20:0.3: The Worship of the Saṅgha or Sakka's Worship
sn11.20:1.2: There the Blessed One said this:
sn11.20:1.3: “Bhikkhus, once in the past Sakka, lord of the devas, addressed his charioteer Mātali thus:
sn11.20:1.4: ‘Harness the chariot with its team of a thousand thoroughbreds, friend Mātali. Let us go to the park grounds to see the beautiful scenery.’
sn11.20:1.5: ‘Yes, your lordship,’ Mātali the charioteer replied. Then he harnessed the chariot with its team of a thousand thoroughbreds and announced to Sakka, lord of the devas:
sn11.20:1.6: ‘The chariot has been harnessed, dear sir.
sn11.20:1.7: You may come at your own convenience.’
sn11.20:1.8: Then, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, descending from the Vejayanta Palace, raised his joined hands in reverential salutation and worshipped the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.
sn11.20:1.9: Then Mātali the charioteer addressed Sakka, lord of the devas, in verse:
sn11.20:2.1: ‘It is these that should worship you—
sn11.20:2.2: The humans stuck in a putrid body,
sn11.20:3.1: Why then do you envy them,
sn11.20:3.3: Tell us about the seers’ conduct;
sn11.20:3.4: Let us hear what you have to say.’
sn11.20:5.1: ‘They do not keep their goods in storage,
sn11.20:5.2: Neither in a pot nor in a box.
sn11.20:5.3: Seeking what has been prepared by others,
sn11.20:5.4: By this they live, firm in vows:
sn11.20:6.1: Those wise ones who give good counsel,
sn11.20:6.4: And people fight with one another,
sn11.20:7.1: Among those who fight, they do not fight;
sn11.20:7.2: Among the violent, they are quenched;
sn11.20:7.3: Among those who grasp, they do not grasp:
sn11.20:7.4: These are the ones whom I worship, Mātali.’
sn11.20:8.2: my lord Sakka, Are indeed the best in the world.
sn11.20:9.4: The chief, climbed into his chariot.”
